properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:31PM MST until November 5 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the San Juan River caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...along the San Juan River from the Four Corners through
Mexican Hat, UT. This includes Bluff, Montezuma Creek and Aneth.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River levels continue to rise due to excess runoff from
Sunday's rainfall. Expect high water levels and the River exceeding
its banks, inundating low-lying areas along the San Juan River. A
prolonged period of high water is forecast, with a crest near 23.5
ft Thursday morning. It will take several hours for all the water
from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1222 PM MST, stream gauge reports upstream and impacts of
flooding have been reported along the San Juan River near
Farmington, NM. Expect flood waters to reach the Four Corners
Wednesday evening and the town of Bluff early Thursday morning.
Timing of crest is subject to change as more details become
available. Please continue to monitor the forecast and updated
warnings.
- At 11:30 AM MST Monday the stage was 20.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 22 feet late this evening with
a secondary crest near 23.5 feet expected near Bluff early
Thursday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Bluff, Montezuma Creek, and Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by earlier excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Merrick County in central Nebraska...
Nance County in central Nebraska...
Polk County in east central Nebraska...
York County in east central Nebraska...
Northern Clay County in south central Nebraska...
Northwestern Fillmore County in south central Nebraska...
Hamilton County in south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of several smaller creeks, streams, and other
low-lying and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring, along
with possible flooding along a few area rivers. Numerous rural
roads likely remain in very poor condition.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 839 PM CST, Various reports along with data from automated
river gauges indicated that mainly minor flooding continues
within various parts of the Warning area, due to a widespread 2-5
inches of rain that fell from Monday into Tuesday. Although
excess water will continue to gradually recede from rural roads
and low-lying areas now that rain has ended and most of the next
several days will be dry, minor flooding will remain possible for
at least another day or two especially along smaller creeks and
streams in the area, along with perhaps a few smaller rivers. In
particular, automated gauges indicate that minor flooding is
possible over the next few days, or perhaps even already
occurring, along the Silver Creek and Prairie Creek in Merrick
and Nance counties, and also along the West Fork Big Blue River
in portions of Hamilton, Fillmore and York counties...including
the McCool Junction area.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Galaway Creek, North Branch Big Blue River, Prairie Slough,
Beaver Creek, Wood River, Stone Creek, Prairie Creek, West Fork
Big Blue River, Lincoln Creek, Timber Creek, School Creek, Clear
Creek, Cottonwood Creek, Plum Creek, Elk Creek, Dry Run Creek,
Warm Slough, Moores Creek.
- Some locations that could experience flooding include...
York, Aurora, Central City, Fullerton, Stromsburg, Harvard,
Genoa, Henderson, Osceola, Shelby, Palmer, Hampton, McCool
Junction, Clarks, Silver Creek, Giltner, Polk, Chapman, Phillips
and Bradshaw.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 4 at 12:53AM CST until November 4 at 2:30AM CST by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out
20 NM...
St. Andrews Bay Waterways...

* Until 230 AM CST.

* At 1252 AM CST, showers capable of producing waterspouts were
located along a line extending from 13 nm south of Panama City
Beach to 23 nm southwest of Mexico Beach, moving north at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Panama City Beach.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 8:13PM MST until November 4 at 2:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 200 PM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. Low-water crossings are
inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 810 PM MST, an upstream floodgate release is causing flooding
along the Salt River.
- Flooding is occurring along the Salt River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Salt River Tubing Recreation Area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring. It is important to know where you are relative
to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become killers in heavy
rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or creeks.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 3:29PM MST until November 6 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande At Alamosa affecting Alamosa County.

.Minor flooding along the Rio Grande through Alamosa is expected due
to upstream flooding occurring in the vicinity of Monte Vista.

For the Rio Grande...including Alamosa...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Alamosa.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon to late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor flooding. Minor agricultural flooding
in low lying areas along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM MST Monday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Wednesday afternoon to a crest of 9.6 feet late Wednesday
evening. It will then fall below flood stage early Thursday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.water.noaa.gov
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

This warning will be in effect until the river falls below its flood
stage.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.
